obligations.note: The change names ticket CHG-26772, a standard ticket. Change manager Erik Brandt approved it on 2026-10-20, before review, and its components (payments.payments, payments.tests) cover both touched paths.
Mara Costa holds change_approver for payments and is not the author (Jonah Weiss). She gave a code_review approval.
The code_review approval names the head commit cae765a1, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json claims a CI run on ci-runner-06 for the head commit, starting 2026-10-21T21:32Z, the same second as the commit. The only attached JUnit report, though, was produced on hostname dev-laptop-7.local at 2026-10-23T20:30Z, two days later, so it is not the output of that CI run. The change description says the suite was green 'locally'. The required CI evidence on the final commit, including the PAY-1 and MC-1 control tests for payments.py, is therefore invalid.
No touched component is security_sensitive: payments.payments and payments.tests are both marked false. No security review is required.
No protected path is touched; the new test file is under apps/baseline-payments/tests/, not tests/controls/. No control_owner approval is required.

required_approvals, is_fully_approved and the policy threshold are unchanged by the diff. The existing exhaustive proof (ledger record ACR-0401) on required_approvals still applies, and the new helper only reports a count.
The ledger entries covering payments.py#required_approvals (ACR-0401) and #release (ACR-0403) are unaffected. The diff only adds a new function, so the covered symbols are unchanged in behaviour.

summary: The code change is small and additive, and the ticket, independent code review and approval coverage are all in order. However, the testing evidence does not hold up. The JUnit report attached as the change's CI output was generated on a developer's Mac two days after the recorded CI run started, so it cannot be the output of the pipeline run named in run.json. With no valid CI report showing the full suite and the touched control tests passing on the head commit, CHG-4 is not met and the change is rejected until a genuine CI run is attached.
